declared.title: Randomized controlled evidence of the efficacy of acceptance and commitment therapy: A systematic review and meta-analysis
declared.foundIn: agent contre-preuve, recherche Crossref / Europe PMC du 2026-11-22 (reports/feeling-bad-about-feeling-bad/counter-evidence.md) ; titre relevé sur Crossref par l'agent : contrôle d'identité plus faible

population: 34 randomized trials of full ACT against established psychotherapies

findings.text: A full acceptance-based therapy (ACT) does no better than other established psychotherapies

support.sentence: Random-effects three-level meta-analyses indicated that full-model ACT was not superior to bona fide psychotherapies on mental and behavioral health outcomes (g = -0.01, p = .86).

limits: ACT is a whole therapy, not acceptance alone
the trials' methods are often weak (no preregistration, low power)
